title: Three-dimensional Foliated Fractional Quantum Hall Phases
claims: Stacks of decoupled ν = 1/3 Laughlin layers (a foliated Laughlin phase) stay stable up to interlayer interactions comparable to the intralayer ones, with a finite extrapolated gap.

In the bilayer, increasing the interlayer pseudopotential V1(1) drives a transition from decoupled Laughlin states to the non-Abelian Fibonacci state, seen in overlaps, torus degeneracy and quasihole counting.
Stacks of two, three and four coupled layers host non-Abelian SU(3)_Nℓ topological order, for which the paper builds explicit CFT model wavefunctions and identifies the spin-TQFT.
With next-nearest-neighbour interlayer interactions, the stack spontaneously breaks layer translation symmetry into a trimerized [1/3 1/3 0] charge pattern.
Within the trimerized sector, the occupied layer pairs form Fibonacci bilayers, so a foliated Fibonacci phase exists in the 9-layer system.
These phases could be realized in layered van der Waals crystals and multilayer heterostructures in strong magnetic fields.
summary: The paper studies stacks of lowest-Landau-level layers at filling 1/3 per layer with truncated Haldane pseudopotential interactions, using exact diagonalization on sphere and torus for up to 10 layers, thin-torus perturbation theory and CFT model wavefunctions. It reports that decoupled Laughlin layers are robust to interlayer coupling, that few-layer stacks host SU(3)_Nℓ non-Abelian orders, and that next-nearest-neighbour interactions can trimerize the stack into a foliated Fibonacci phase.
strengths: It is the first exact-diagonalization study of quantum Hall multilayers well beyond four layers, combining sphere and torus ED, thin-torus analysis, CFT wavefunctions and Monte Carlo overlaps.

It gives an explicit, general CFT construction of SU(Nℓ)_k multilayer wavefunctions with a spin-TQFT identification, and generalized SU(3)_Nℓ exclusion rules checked layer multiplet by multiplet against ED spectra.

The bilayer analysis is consistent across sphere and torus, with the 9-to-6 torus degeneracy change, quasihole counting and the rejection of the interlayer Pfaffian agreeing with one another and with earlier work.

A transparent thin-torus mapping shows that interlayer pseudopotentials generate correlated pair hopping that maps onto a transverse-field Ising model, and the paper is candid about open questions such as the unidentified D = 3 torus region.

issues.headline: Layer charge-density wave may be an artifact of truncated short-range interaction
issues.issue: With only V1(0) intralayer, moving electrons between layers at filling ≤ 1/3 costs no intralayer energy, and the truncated pseudopotentials drop the long-range tails that give the capacitive (Hartree) cost of a period-3 layer-density modulation, which for d ≲ l_B is comparable to the FQH and quasihole gaps. The classical argument of Eqs. 24–25 assumes an intralayer cost the ED Hamiltonian lacks and needs a negative layer kernel that a real Coulomb interaction with neutralizing background does not give, so the foliated Fibonacci phase currently holds only for the pseudopotential model.

evidence.quote: In this work we have shown ED results for short-range pseudopotential interactions. Studying the stability of the phases we have found when including a long-range tail of the interaction in Eq. (30) is an area which deserves future study.
evidence.location: Sec. V B1 (Eqs. 24–25), Fig. 7(a,b), Fig. S5, Sec. VI B

issues.fix: State where the neutralizing charge sits, and repeat the sector competition of Figs. 7(a,b) and S5 and the analysis of Eq. (24) with at least V3(0), ideally a longer Coulomb-derived tail or the full projected Coulomb interaction, including or estimating the Hartree energy of the layer-density modulation for realistic d/l_B and comparing it with the trimerization gain and quasihole gaps. If the [1/3 1/3 0] region does not survive, reframe the claim as a property of the short-range model and say which ingredient (for example dielectric engineering) could make λ(2π/3) < 0.
issues.fix_scoped: Restrict the trimerization and foliated Fibonacci claim to the truncated short-range pseudopotential model, stating that it may not survive long-range Coulomb interactions.

edit_scoped.before: By focusing on the case of filling ν = 1/3 of the lowest Landau level in each layer, we show that (i) the limit of decoupled Laughlin states is stable upon introducing interlayer interactions and (ii) the system can enter a spontaneously layer-trimerized foliated non-Abelian Fibonacci phase.
edit_scoped.after: By focusing on the case of filling ν = 1/3 of the lowest Landau level in each layer, we show that (i) the limit of decoupled Laughlin states is stable upon introducing interlayer interactions and (ii) for short-range pseudopotential interactions truncated to the leading intralayer and interlayer terms, the system can enter a layer-trimerized foliated non-Abelian Fibonacci phase.

issues.headline: Trimerization largely fixed by commensurability; uniform competitor absent at Nℓ = 9
issues.issue: For Nℓ = 9 (Ne = 12, Nφ = 3) the uniform [2/9 2/9 2/9] configuration cannot occur, and with Nφ = 3 the [220]^3 arrangement is essentially forced, so the larger trimerized region is partly built into the choice of system; for Nℓ = 6 the sectors are compared at one Nφ that sits at the Laughlin shift for [330] but not for the uniform sector. Without tunneling, layer particle numbers are conserved, so the three-fold degeneracy in Fig. 8(c,d) is a translation degeneracy of superselection sectors that holds by construction and does not test dynamical symmetry breaking.

evidence.quote: In the Nℓ = 9 system, the trimerized phase occupies a larger region as there is no competing state with homogeneous filling at that total particle number
evidence.location: Sec. V B3, Fig. 7(a,b), Fig. 8(c,d), Fig. S5

issues.fix: Provide a size series in which the uniform competitor is present and both sectors have a candidate FQH state at the appropriate shift, compare energies per particle with background-charge and shift corrections and show the size trend, ideally repeat the competition on the torus, and add a small interlayer tunneling to the Nℓ = 6 ED to show the k_z = 2π/3 layer-density modulation survives. Until then, qualify "spontaneously layer-trimerized" (abstract) and "appears to be robust" (end of Sec. V B3).
issues.fix_scoped: State that for Nℓ = 9 the uniform competitor is excluded by the choice of particle number, so the trimerized region there partly reflects that choice and not demonstrated spontaneous trimerization.

edit_scoped.before: In the Nℓ = 9 system, the trimerized phase occupies a larger region as there is no competing state with homogeneous filling at that total particle number (since Ne = 12 is not divisible by Nℓ = 9).
edit_scoped.after: In the Nℓ = 9 system, no state with homogeneous filling exists at this total particle number (since Ne = 12 is not divisible by Nℓ = 9), so the larger trimerized region there partly reflects the choice of system size rather than demonstrating spontaneous trimerization.

issues.headline: Foliated Fibonacci identification rests on 2+2 quasihole counting only
issues.issue: In the Nℓ = 9 calculation each Fibonacci bilayer is a 2+2 system in 4 orbitals, where Fibonacci counting (D0 ⊕ D2) differs from decoupled Laughlin (D0 ⊕ D1 ⊕ D2) by a single L = 1 multiplet, and the paper does not show that competing shift-3 bilayer states give different counting at these sizes. Δ_QH in Fig. 7(c,d) is not defined precisely, the Nℓ = 6 overlap of the blue counting region with the gapped trimerized region is never plotted, and there is no gap scaling or torus degeneracy for the foliated Fibonacci phase.

evidence.quote: Specifically, we show that the foliated Fibonacci phase exists in the 9-layer system with pseudopotential interactions within and between neighboring layers.
evidence.location: Abstract; Figs. 7(b–d), 8, S5

issues.fix: Define Δ_QH; give the predicted quasihole counting of competing bilayer states at 2+2, Nφ = 4 and 3+3, Nφ = 7; plot the intersection of trimerized and Fibonacci-counting regions for Nℓ = 6; compute overlaps of the Nℓ = 6 and 9 ground states with products of bilayer Fibonacci wavefunctions and with products of Ψ_330, Ψ_PSS, Laughlin or ED bilayer states; where feasible add a larger per-layer size; and give the torus ground-state degeneracy of a trimerized stack.
issues.fix_scoped: Describe the 9-layer result as quasihole counting consistent with a foliated Fibonacci phase at two electrons per occupied layer, not as an established phase.

edit_scoped.before: Specifically, we show that the foliated Fibonacci phase exists in the 9-layer system with pseudopotential interactions within and between neighboring layers.
edit_scoped.after: Specifically, we find quasihole counting consistent with a foliated Fibonacci phase in a 9-layer system with two electrons per occupied layer and pseudopotential interactions within and between neighboring layers.

issues.headline: Fibonacci parameter regime never placed against realistic Coulomb interactions
issues.issue: Sec. II A says all phases appear in parameter space obeying physical inequalities, yet Sec. For LLL Coulomb, V0/V1 ≈ 2 places the system in the S = 1 / singlet region or on the decoupled-Laughlin / (112) boundary of Figs. 2–3, and the truncation drops V3(0), V2(1) and V1(2).

issues.headline: Foliated Laughlin gap extrapolation unjustified and tests only two-particle limit
issues.issue: Fig. 5(a) uses 2 electrons per layer, where the intralayer L = 0 state is unique, so the near-unit overlap cannot distinguish Laughlin layers from weakly correlated states. The Δ∞ ≈ 0.37 extrapolation uses a b/Nℓ form that Table S6 contradicts (gap constant in Nℓ from Nℓ = 4), is dominated by N = 2 points, ignores the spread of per-Nℓ fits (0.596 to 0.461), is done at one interaction point, and omits interlayer charge-transfer excitations in other sectors.

evidence.quote: First, decoupled Laughlin layers remain stable against interlayer interactions up to strengths comparable to the intralayer interactions.
evidence.location: Sec. I C; Fig. 5(a,b); App. L, Eq. (S124), Table S6

issues.fix: Include neighbouring per-layer sectors in Δ; fit at fixed Nℓ ≥ 4 using only N ≥ 3 and quote fit uncertainties; use the largest N per layer for Nℓ ≥ 3; give the uncoupled single-layer reference gap; extrapolate along a cut toward the boundary and show how the Laughlin / (112) boundary moves with N and Nℓ; and state that the Nℓ = 10 overlap map tests only the two-particle limit.
issues.fix_scoped: Claim only that, at the one interaction point studied, the foliated Laughlin gap stays finite in small systems, with the large-Nℓ overlap map limited to two particles per layer.

edit_scoped.before: First, decoupled Laughlin layers remain stable against interlayer interactions up to strengths comparable to the intralayer interactions.
edit_scoped.after: First, decoupled Laughlin layers remain gapped against interlayer interactions of moderate strength in the finite systems we can study, although for many layers our data are limited to two particles per layer.

issues.headline: Tunneling, density control and disorder omitted though trimerization needs charge transfer
issues.issue: The model has no single-particle tunneling, yet tunneling drives the Laughlin-to-Fibonacci transition in Ref. 84, mixes particle-per-layer sectors and favours the uniform configuration, and for d ≲ l_B it is not obviously small compared with sub-meV FQH gaps. Filling 1/3 at 10 T needs about 8 × 10^10 cm^-2 per layer from intrinsic doping with matching disorder, and in a 3D crystal the average filling is tuned only by B.

evidence.quote: Although our model does not include interlayer tunneling, the physical realization of the layer-translational symmetry-breaking state should include a small tunneling between the layers to allow charge redistribution.
evidence.location: Sec. V B; Sec. VI A

issues.fix: Estimate the tunneling scale at which the [1/3 1/3 0] state is destabilized (for example by second-order perturbation theory between sectors) relative to the computed gaps in meV; estimate tunneling scales and required doping homogeneity for the proposed platforms; and say over what range of average filling around 2/9 the trimerized state remains the ground state.
issues.fix_scoped: State that the effect of interlayer tunneling on the trimerized state is not determined, since tunneling also mixes particle-per-layer sectors and can drive the Laughlin-to-Fibonacci transition.

edit_scoped.before: The FFQH phases we obtain are gapped, and hence they are stable as long as the strength of the tunneling is much smaller than the gap.
edit_scoped.after: The FFQH phases we obtain are gapped, but tunneling also mixes particle-per-layer sectors and can itself drive the Laughlin-to-Fibonacci transition, so the tunneling scale up to which the trimerized state survives remains to be determined.
